title: Pressão de pneus por terreno: como testar sem transformar sensação em dado

confirmed_facts.soft_terrain_pressure_range_bar: 1.5–2.0 bar (22–29 psi) for 2.3–2.5" wide MTB tires, per Specialized guide.
confirmed_facts.hardpacked_terrain_pressure_range_bar: 2.2–2.7 bar (32–39 psi) for the same width, per Trek recommendations.
confirmed_facts.pressure_adjustment_step_bar: Adjust in increments of 0.1–0.2 bar (1.5–3 psi) and record handling notes after each lap.
confirmed_facts.recording_method: Use a portable pressure gauge and a field notebook or a cycling app (e.g., Strava) to log pressure, terrain, rider feeling and lap time.
confirmed_facts.rolling_resistance_effect: Lower pressure (≈1.5 bar) increases rolling resistance by ~5–8 % on smooth hard‑pack, according to Continental technical data.
confirmed_facts.lateral_stability_effect: Higher pressure (≈2.7 bar) improves cornering stability on technical climbs, as described in Schwalbe’s tire performance guide.
confirmed_facts.impact_absorption_effect: Reducing pressure by 0.3 bar improves vibration damping on rocky sections by ~10 % (Schwalbe), without excessive rim stress.
confirmed_facts.width_pressure_correlation: Wider tires (2.5") can run 0.3–0.5 bar lower than narrower (2.0") for equivalent grip, per Continental recommendations.

limitations: Não há dados de teste de campo específicos publicados no blog da TheBiker.
Os valores são médias gerais; peso do ciclista, carga e geometria da bicicleta podem exigir ajustes individuais.
As recomendações dos fabricantes são baseadas em condições padrão e podem não refletir terrenos extremos ou clima muito quente/frio.
